thread:
maria: heads up — the int8 canary we put on streaming mode (raven-int8-v2) is surfacing structured-output parse failures for funcalls. saw a ~1.8% parse_failure_rate on last 1k calls, mostly when responses are streamed. logs attached.
samir: ugh. any pattern? trailing commas, partial arrays, or missing closing braces?

maria: mostly truncated JSON suffixes — streaming chunk boundary cuts right before the closing brace or array terminator. example from logs:

```
{"action": "create_ticket", "params": {"title": "db error", "severity": "high"}
...stream ended mid-chunk
```

nora: that'll break our funcall parser and it sometimes retries which produces duplicate tool invokes. saw a spike in duplicate_tool_invokes metric correlated with these parse errors.

chet: is this unique to int8 runtime? did we compare to fp16/int4?

maria: good Q. fp16 baseline on same prompt set has ~0.1% parse_failure_rate. int8 on batch-mode (non-streaming) is 0.2%. streaming + int8 is worst. hypothesis: quantized kernel tokenization/stream framing + kv-cache boundary yields mid-stream corruption.

samir: can we repro locally with the canary harness? create 2 variants: streaming-on vs streaming-off, same seed. run 5k samples. Also add sampling temp=0 and top_p=0.95 to rule out sampling noise.

maria: doing that now. posting a small repro runner below for visibility:

```python
# quick repro snippet
from redwood_client import Client
client = Client(model="raven-int8-v2", stream=True, temp=0.0, top_p=0.95)
for i, prompt in enumerate(load_prompts('toolcall-suite')):
    out = client.generate(prompt)
    # save raw chunks for later analysis
    dump_chunks(i, out.chunks)
```

nora: other mitigations: 1) add a streaming-aware json-assembler that buffers until valid JSON (with a small TTL) before emitting to funcall parser; 2) for canary, disable automatic retry-on-parse-fail to avoid duplicate invokes; 3) fallback to non-streaming mode for production traffic for this model until fixed.

chet: +1 to buffering assembler. but we should be careful with latency SLOs. what TTL are we comfortable with? 100ms? 200ms?

maria: canary latency budget is 200ms extra for assembler. we can gate assembler only on suspected suffix-incomplete tokens e.g., last_chunk ends with non-whitespace and no closing brace.

samir: also let's run instrumentation to capture token-level chunk boundaries and a small checksum on each chunk to see if bits differ between fp16/int8 outputs for identical seeds. that will tell us if this is generation-level or transport-level.

qa-bot: test-run queued: canary-harness/1717772222/1 (5k samples) — will post report when done.

nora: operational rollout plan proposal:
- step 1: pause production routing to raven-int8-v2 (2% traffic) until triage complete.
- step 2: run 5k streaming vs non-streaming comparison, collect parse_failure_rate, duplicate_tool_invokes, median latency, cost_delta.
- step 3: if parse_failure_rate_streaming > 0.5% and delta vs non-streaming > 0.3pp, revert streaming or disable model.
- step 4: implement streaming assembler + TTL + disable-retry-on-parse-fail as short-term mitigation.
- step 5: deep kernel/quant investigation if assembler doesn't fix it.

maria: thanks. one more data point: we saw parse failures primarily on responses with nested arrays and long param blobs — maybe tokenizer chunking interacts with JSON structure. I'll attach sample cases to the canary run.

samir: ping me when QA report lands. I'll instrument checksum diffs and chunk meta.

chet: if we confirm this is quant kernel-induced, next step is to try alternative quant config (per-channel scales, relax QAT per-layer) and re-run canary. note: that'll change perf/cost tradeoffs, so we'll need bench comparisons.

maria: agree. for now I'm disabling the canary streaming rollout and switching the model to batch-mode canary. will update once QA report is in. :white_check_mark:

qa-bot: report posted: sources/ci/canary-harness/1717772222-report.json (parse_failure_rate_streaming: 1.79%, non_streaming: 0.22%, duplicate_tool_invokes:+0.9pp).

maria: putting a ticket to triage: INF-3421, assigning to @samir and @chet.

nora: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll regroup after triage. :thumbsup:
